title: Optimal-Depth Sorting Networks (n = 9..16): minimize parallel depth
description: Pure Lean 4.36.0 (zero Mathlib) certified optimization of minimum-depth parallel sorting networks on n = 9..16 wires, with pairwise wire disjointness, simultaneous 1-cycle layer semantics, Knuth’s Zero-One Principle, and a bit-sliced 2^n-input evaluator formally proved inside `SortDepth/Spec.lean`. Eight independent hill-climb tracks start from textbook Odd-Even Transposition Sort seeds (depths 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16) and target the proven minimum parallel depths D(n) (7, 7, 8, 8, 9, 9, 9, 9; Parberry 1989, Bundala–Závodný 2014), pinned to `bertdobbelaere/SorterHunter@3d8b345` (MIT).

tasks.title: Minimize 9-wire sorting network depth (baseline 9)
tasks.description: Submit a layered parallel comparator network on 9 wires in `SortDepth/Layers9.lean` (`SortDepth.depth9` and `SortDepth.layers9`), seeded with textbook Odd-Even Transposition Sort (depth 9; proven optimum: 7, Parberry 1989). Frozen `SortDepth/Bound9.lean` kernel-verifies in-bounds ordered comparators (`i < j < 9`), pairwise disjoint wires within every layer, exact layer count, and sorting on all 2^9 = 512 Boolean inputs via `decide +kernel`, lifting to every linear order by the formalized Zero-One Principle in `SortDepth/Spec.lean`. Only strict improvements below the current record earn credit.
